title: They were nailing Him to wood…
paragraphs:
They were nailing Him to wood…
and He was speaking mercy.
Before you scroll—this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because the people He was praying for… didn’t feel sorry.

They weren’t repenting.
They weren’t kneeling.
They were laughing. Mocking. Driving the nails deeper.
“Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” (Luke 23:34)
Let that wreck you for a second.

Because we love forgiveness…
as long as it comes after apology.

We love grace…
as long as the person deserves it.

He releases forgiveness in the middle of violence.
In the middle of injustice.
In the middle of being misunderstood, rejected, and publicly shamed.
And here’s the part most people avoid:
That prayer wasn’t just for them.

Because if we’re honest—deep, uncomfortable, no-filter honest—
we have lived like enemies of God.

We didn’t crucify Him with iron…
we crucified Him with indifference.
That quiet shame no one else sees.
The version of you that smiles in public but avoids God in private.
The part of your story you hope never gets exposed.
This is where the Gospel stops being theory and starts becoming rescue.
Because Luke 23:34 is not just a sentence.
It’s a window into the heart of God.
Jesus is not denying their sin.
He’s saying, “They don’t fully see what they’re doing.”

Some scholars interpret this as spiritual blindness—
that sin has so clouded the human heart that we don’t grasp the full weight of our rebellion.
And that’s exactly what sin does.
It convinces you that distance from God is normal.
Until one day… you feel it.
The cross is not just where Jesus suffered.
It’s where He stood in your place.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Not when you promised to change.
While you were still in it.
That’s when He made a way.

Those words—“Father, forgive them”—
were paid for with blood.
Your forgiveness is not God pretending your sin didn’t happen.
It’s God placing your sin on Jesus.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness.” (1 Peter 2:24)
Forgiveness is not something you earn.
You cannot receive what you refuse to admit you need.
And many people stay stuck here.
But Jesus doesn’t just forgive you.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)

Because the same voice that said,
“Father, forgive them”—
So what are you still holding onto?
That pride that refuses to bow?

There is no sin too dark
for the blood of Christ.

If He could pray for His executioners—
He can forgive you.
Let the cross be the place where your shame dies and your new life begins.
And when you receive that kind of mercy—
Because grace didn’t just touch you.
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
And if this stirred something deep inside you…
